name: Conditional & Hedging Usage
description: Analyzes the frequency and complexity of conditional sentence patterns (e.g., 'If X, then Y' or hypothetical structures).
algorithm: Hypothetical Syntax Profiling & Conditional Marker Extraction
mechanism: Commercial Large Language Models are heavily penalized during training for making absolute, definitive statements, especially regarding facts, advice, or future predictions. To maintain 'safety' and nuance, they rely obsessively on conditional logic and hypothetical hedging ('If', 'In the event that', 'Should you decide', 'Unless'). Their conditional structures are also geometrically perfect, strictly pairing an 'if' clause with a flawless 'then/would/could' resolution. Human writers, conversely, are often bolder, more declarative, and frequently construct fractured or incomplete conditional thoughts. This method extracts and evaluates the density of these conditional markers and maps their syntactic resolution. A high frequency of perfectly resolved, overly cautious conditional statements strongly flags the 'helpful, harmless, and honest' alignment typical of modern AI.
useCase: Detecting AI-generated advisory articles, legal or medical disclaimers, opinion pieces, and answers that refuse to take a definitive stance by hiding behind excessive hypothetical scenarios.
strengths:
• Highly effective at detecting the inherent 'fence-sitting' and non-committal nature of RLHF-aligned AI models.
• Scales excellently across different languages, as the syntactic function of conditionality exists globally.
• Fast to compute, relying on dependency parsing rather than heavy semantic embeddings.
limitations:
• Susceptible to false positives in genuine legal documents, scientific hypotheses, or deeply technical manuals where heavy conditional logic is actually required.
• Can be bypassed if a user explicitly prompts the AI to write with 'absolute certainty' and 'no hedging'.
• Less effective on narrative fiction where hypothetical scenarios are naturally less common.
parameters:
Analysis: Conditional Clause Extraction
Metric: Density of Hypothetical Markers & Resolution Symmetry
Output: 0-100 Conditional Hedging (Non-Committal) Score
accuracy: High — 75-85% on advisory, analytical, or QA-style text. Efficacy drops on highly assertive creative writing.

references.title: Jurafsky, D. & Martin, J.H. (2024). Speech and Language Processing. 3rd Edition.
Uchendu, A. et al. (2020). Authorship Attribution for Neural Text Generation. EMNLP.
